rationale: Bounded preregistered real-arrival predictability diagnostic, one minute bins and 1/5/10-minute forecast horizons before inspecting held-out forecast results. Horizons cover existing 1-/5-minute observation scales and a longer engineering lookahead, not a claimed optimal maintenance horizon. Persistence and daily/weekly seasonal forecasts derive solely from actual past counts; learned Poisson histogram boosting uses past lag/rolling counts and calendar clock features, never completed-query resource profiles or the replay future. Small fixed depth/leaf/iteration settings provide a reproducible low-capacity first diagnostic, with no hyperparameter/test-window search, clipping or acceptance threshold. First-week training and three subsequent reserved days fixed by audited cohort protocol; test windows wholly held out, no horizon crosses a split. Prior evaluated counts become available chronologically as past observations. No random internal validation, conformal coverage claim, scheduler/cost-model fit, normalized intensity or Model C promotion. CPU limit is operational. Limited weekly cycles and overlapping horizons prevent publication-grade independence/uncertainty claims.
